I5.quote: The hydrogen storage properties of carbon single-wall and multi-wall nanotubes (SWNTs and MWNTs), graphitic nanofibers, and other nanostructured carbons have recently become the subject of considerable debate.

notes: I1 fails on the TPD-alone clause. Hydrogen amounts come only from TPD: 'The temperature programmed desorption (TPD) apparatus employed to determine the hydrogen capacities of the various carbon-based materials has been previously described' (main, p. 2, Experimental Details); 'the integrated area of the hydrogen desorption peak centered at ~ 375 K In Fig. 2 a) corresponds to a hydrogen adsorption capacity of < 1 wt%' (main, p. 5, Results and Discussion). Fig. 2 plots 'Hydrogen TPD Mass Signal (a.u.)' against temperature (main, p. 4). The 'in-house volumetric technique' (main, p. 3) only confirmed the TPD calibration against CaH2, TiH2 and Pd; it is not an H2 uptake measurement on the carbon samples. Not theoretical and not electrochemical (gas-phase room-temperature H2 exposure at 500 torr), so the I1 failure is coded no_conditions_stated. not_primary does not apply: an MRS Symposium Proceedings paper reporting original TPD and TEM data. retracted: record is_retracted false and no retraction notice in the PDF. duplicate_data: no statement that the values were published before. For the record, no specific surface area is reported for any sample either.
